topic: Local-first sync tools: what exists, what works, common weaknesses
question: What distinguishes sync tools that keep users from the ones that stall, and what do app stores require of them?

observation.statement: Store guidance requires apps that process user data off-device to disclose it, and shows the disclosure automatically when the privacy manifest declares it.

findings.hypothesis: A disclosed sync feature loses little adoption relative to an undisclosed one, because the disclosure is shown either way once the manifest declares it.

recommendation.statement: Treat the disclosure as a product feature rather than a cost, and declare it explicitly in the manifest instead of waiting for it to be inferred.

observation.statement: Issue trackers of several large sync tools are dominated by conflict-resolution bugs rather than by feature requests.

findings.hypothesis: Conflict handling, not sync speed, is the dominant reason users abandon sync tools.

recommendation.statement: Spend the first phases on deterministic conflict resolution before any performance work.

sources.title: Developer policy: data use and disclosure
Why do sync tools plateau?
sources.note: Anecdotal; supports an observation, not a high-confidence recommendation on its own.

gaps: No reliable public figures for retention by tool category; the adoption claims above are directional only.

disagreements: Rates the disclosure reach penalty as unknown rather than small.
